children: By Staff Writer

Oman’s Ministry of Agricultural, Fisheries, Wealth and Water Resources has received 14 bids for the construction of the Wadi Al Khawd Flood Protection Dam in Muscat Governorate, according to tender board data.
The financial bids were opened on 14 September 2026, with China’s China International Water and Electric Corporation submitting the lowest offer at 48.57 million Omani rials ($126.2 million).

Turkey’s Eksen Project Construction Tourism and Trade submitted the second-lowest bid at OMR57.50 million ($149.55 million), followed by compatriot Ozkar Construction Industry and Trade at OMR 57.74 million ($150.17 million).
Other bidders in ascending order are as follows:
· Oman’s United Thumrait Lines at OMR 57.77 million ($150.25 million)
· Turkey’s Portex Construction Industry and Trade OMR 59.65 million $155.14 million
· Oman’s Galfar Engineering and Contracting OMR 59.70 million ($155.27 million)
· Oman’s The Arab Contractors Oman OMR 61.59 million ($160.18 million)
· Turkey’s Yildizlar Construction and Trade OMR 66.35 million ($172.56 million)
· India’s Hindustan Construction Company OMR 70.25 million ($182.71 million)
· Oman’s Strabag Oman OMR 79.37 million ($206.43 million)
· Oman’s AZ Engineers and Partners OMR 89.16 million ($231.89 million)
· Oman’s Sarooj Construction Company OMR 89.60 million ($233.03 million)
· Egypt’s Egyptian Contracting Co & Partner OMR 92.27 million ($239.98 million)
· Oman’s Al Adrak Trading and Contracting OMR 150.38 million ($391.11 million)
Tender documents went on sale on 20 May 2026, while bid submissions closed on 14 September, followed by the opening of the priced bids on the same day.
In August 2026, Zawya Projects had reported that Oman is likely to award the dam construction contract in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The Wadi Al Khawd flood protection dam (AK01 dam) is located just upstream of the Al Khawd village, according to project details shared by the ministry. The proposed site is on the boundary between the hilly midland and flat coastal plain. A widening of the right bank terrace located upstream the proposed dam axis is providing a favourable topographic basin for storage. The access to the right bank is from the Al Khawd village. Crossing the wadi bed is usually possible with a 4WD except when the base flow is high during some days or weeks after rainfall. The reservoir area is in a remote and harsh area. The access is only possible by walking or driving in the wadi bed when the base flow is low. It is not possible to reach Fanjah because of a narrow and rocky section about 3 km upstream from the dam axis.
(Writing by Deva Palanisamy; Editing by Anoop Menon)
